October 10: Yet another unwanted visit.

At this point, I'm genuinely questioning whether the word "NO" exists in their vocabulary, or whether they simply believe their religion gives them permission to disregard it.

Let's make something perfectly clear: Your religious beliefs do not entitle you to my time, my attention, my property, or my consent.

When someone explicitly tells you they are not interested, that is not an invitation to return and try again. It is a boundary. Your refusal to respect that boundary is not devotion, kindness, or some noble religious mission. It is harassment masquerading as righteousness.

The sheer arrogance of believing your faith somehow overrides another person's right to be left alone is astounding.

Consent is not a concept reserved for sexual encounters. It applies to personal boundaries, too. And repeatedly forcing unwanted religious conversations on people who have already refused is not spreading love. It is demonstrating a spectacular lack of respect.

Your right to practise your religion ends where my right to refuse your advances begins.

Stop knocking. Stop preaching. And learn that NO IS A COMPLETE SENTENCE.

I provided 100% of the required information for a wire

I paid the fee, verified all the info that they wrote down, and then asked why the reference number wasnt in the place of "customer code" on the wire transfer receipt.

I was told that its nothing to be concerned about, and that they have the reference code on their end and I just cant see it because it doesnt get printed out.

Now 4 days later the wire has been rejected and returned to my account because it actually did NOT include a reference number, and now it has an additional fee taken off of it and im being told theres nothing that can be done.

So now I have to take both the fees and the delay which ended up costing me probably close to another $800.

For how much they make from just holding my money alone I cant imagine 85 dollars in fees breaking the bank for their side of the bargain. I cant be banking here much longer if this is the arrangement.

TERRIBLE!!!

My access card compromised on a Friday morning. I can't get to the branch until Saturday afternoon. I call customer service / fraud department at 2:50pm as I'm heading to the branch.

I'm disabled with mobility issues and use a walker for shopping and longer distances. Due to a frozen access card I can't use Uber. The buses takes 45 minutes. I arrive at 3:42. I wait ten minutes in line. I'm told the branch closes in 5 minutes, it's actually 8 minutes and COME BACK MONDAY!!!

I have no cash and my account is frozen. I can't even e-transfer to a friend. I can't use Uber due to the frozen account and I don't have cash for a taxi. I get caught in a torrential rainstorm on the way home.

Terrible way to treat a handicapped customer paying $31 a month in service charges.

I open a PC Financial account online in ten minutes. No service charges for the same services I was receiving. The exception is for the safety deposit box included in my monthly account fee. I haven't been able to use this benefit because they don't have any safety deposit boxes available at this branch.

Bottom line, there are choices investigate them, mine is Presidents Choice Financial.

p.s. The banks know, as they do studies and surveys, most customers won't change accounts when they screw up or screw you over. That's why they don't care. You're the customer take your business someplace else. Money talks and BS (Bad Service) made me walk!

Monday, 24 August 2026 Update.

TD Bank posted a response to the review.

I sent a copy of this review to TD Banks Senior Customer Care Office via email (Google it, you can't post email addresses in reviews). I received an email back today and a phone call. They said that this should not have happened in the phone conversation and a letter should been given to any client when service is refused, they did not.

Today, staff at the branch provided me with the new access card and were quite helpful. I received the service I should have had on Saturday. The staff that were in on Saturday were not there today. I left a message with the staff to please have the branch manager call me to discuss the matter. The representative on the phone today offered me $50 account credit for the poor service and transportation  expenses. It is something.

The lesson is still the same, we are customers and complaining can bring one some satisfaction and resolution. I hope this helps someone not to have the same or similar situation occur.

Your consumer advocate,

This is by far the worst All You Can Eat restaurant I’ve ever been to in Canada.

I’ve heard of similar restaurants having a 2-hour or 2.5-hour time limit, but this place actually limits each person to only 20 pieces of sashimi. What’s even more ridiculous is that there were only about three tables occupied in the entire restaurant, yet we still had to wait a very long time for our food.

The salmon was sliced extremely thin and the pieces were ridiculously small. The menu clearly stated that certain sushi items came in 6–8 pieces, but we only received 4–5 pieces. There were even times when what we received was completely different from what we had ordered.

We placed two rounds of orders. When we placed our second order, the server noticeably hinted that we shouldn’t order any more food and said something along the lines of, “This is the last time we’re serving you.” Honestly, that was extremely uncomfortable, especially at an All You Can Eat restaurant.

Overall, this is genuinely the worst All You Can Eat experience I’ve ever had.

If the $25.99 price is what attracts you, I sincerely recommend spending an extra $15 per person and going somewhere else. At least you won’t end up ruining the rest of your day just to save a few dollars, right?

one_star_reviews.text:
I recently purchased a choke tube that was specifically recommended to me by an employee for my particular firearm. I trusted their expertise and purchased the product based on their recommendation.

After using it while hunting, I noticed an excessive amount of black plastic residue. I removed the choke tube and inspected it more closely, only to discover that the choke tube I was sold and told was compatible with my firearm was not the correct or compatible choke tube for my gun. This appears to be the reason for the excessive residue.

I returned to the store to discuss my concern, expecting that since the product was specifically selected and recommended by their employee for my firearm, they would take responsibility and make the situation right. Unfortunately, that was not the case.

I was offered a small store credit, but only if I put it toward purchasing the correct choke tube — the correct product that I should have been sold in the first place. I don’t feel that is a reasonable resolution when I relied on the employee’s recommendation and expertise.

What makes this even more disappointing is that as a Weatherby dealer, yet the staff were unable to properly identify which product was compatible with my Weatherby firearm. If you’re going to sell and represent a specific brand, customers should be able to trust that the employees have a basic understanding of the products they’re selling.

Mistakes can happen, but what matters is how a business handles them. In this case, I don’t feel the issue was properly acknowledged or resolved.

I trusted that the staff knew their firearms and the products they sell, but unfortunately, this experience proved otherwise. I will not be shopping at a store that provides incorrect information to customers and then refuses to take responsibility when that information results in a problem.

I have been a patient at Stonegate Community Health Centre for over 20 years, and I am really disappointed with the experience I had with one of the receptionists.

I received an appointment reminder email and when I tried to confirm my appointment, I got a message saying that my appointment could not be found and that I needed to call the clinic because it may have been moved or cancelled.

When I called to find out what happened, the receptionist told me that I had called the day before and cancelled my appointment because I wasn’t feeling well. I told her several times that I never called and never cancelled my appointment. Instead of listening to me, she kept talking over me and insisting that she had spoken to me personally. She then told me that I was being rude, when I was simply trying to understand how my appointment had been cancelled.

I thought maybe she had confused me with one of my many family members who also go to Stonegate, so I asked most of them if they had called the day before. None of them had called or cancelled my appointment. I also explained to her that my parents would never call to cancel an appointment on my behalf.

What really concerns me is that my appointment was cancelled or changed after someone called, but it doesn’t seem like there was proper confirmation of who that person actually was. I should be the one cancelling or making changes to my appointment. This is a privacy concern and I think the clinic needs to make sure they are properly confirming who they are speaking to before making changes to someone’s appointment.

The receptionist continued talking over me and insisting that she had spoken to me, even though I repeatedly told her she had not. She eventually hung up on me while I was still talking.

This also isn’t the first bad experience that either myself or one of my parents has had with this receptionist. My mother’s first language is not English, and I have personally seen this receptionist become impatient and disrespectful when she has difficulty understanding someone whose first language isn’t English. My mother has experienced this herself.

Everyone deserves to be treated with patience and respect, especially when they may have difficulty communicating in English.

After being a patient at Stonegate for over 20 years, I am honestly very disappointed with how this was handled. I hope the clinic looks into what happened and takes concerns about professionalism, communication, patient privacy and properly confirming a patient’s identity seriously.

Really disappointing.

For the last year, Sarducci West has been a go to. It’s not cheap, so for special occasions it’s my family’s favourite. On Wednesday evening, my family placed a $60 order for a birthday. Half my items were missing when they arrived. This was a small order. The bread sticks were burned and BLACK. How they were allowed to leave the kitchen, I have no clue.

When I called in to tell them about my missing items and burnt sticks, the lady at the other end of the phone was apologetic and said they would send out the missing/burnt items right away. She absolutely knew about the bread sticks before I mentioned them.

By the time the replacements came (over an hour later) the panzerotti’s that were first delivered sat in my oven to keep warm so our whole order could be eaten together (that’s what I paid $60 for). After an hour of sitting around, the panzerotti’s didn’t taste the same.  It would have been really nice if the lady who was supposedly going to “rush” the replacements out had clued into the fact that my panzarotti’s (part of the original order) would be sitting around for over an additional hour while she took her time getting here.

When I asked the apologetic lady that was so helpful at first, that I would like to speak to the owner, she told me he would be in on Friday. I left a message for him. No one called back, so I called in again. A man told me Chris the owner wasn’t in on Friday, he should be in Sunday. When I called in today (Sunday) the same lady, now a bit condescending, miraculously couldn’t tell me when Chris would be in.

Yes, Sarducci replaced the missing and burnt items (an hour later) and apologized (thank you) but your 2 mistakes costed my family the enjoyment of our $60 meal. You didn’t offer to replace my full order or refund my order. You didn’t prioritize getting the missing/burnt items to us. Instead, *if* in the future I want to place another order, you could offer 20% off. There’s being stingy and then there’s just being difficult and not owning up to your mistakes (on my family’s dime).

So, Chris read your Google Review’s I guess because messages aren’t getting thru to you and your kitchen needs some better management and quality control. It’s a real blessing to live in a town where there’s a pizza place on each block.

My son has an opioid addiction, we almost lost him last year. He was 11 months clean and relapsed in June. I talked to Into Action and they sounded like they had an OK program and have been around for a long time. I also ASSUMED the rooms and food would be better, they were not. The food is being delivered every day, not cooked in house, which is a huge surprise for my son, not the quality we expected.

They picked him up and took him to the home. Once he arrived, they made him sign their contracts, he was so high he was not capable reading or signing anything. Their contract states they were supposed to search his items, which they did not and left stuff on him, also in the contract was that they took his phone away for 7 days (very important part) on day 5 he calls me BECAUSE THEY GAVE HIM HIS PHONE, and says he is leaving, they have basically left him in a room for days detoxing by himself. So, he leaves…… I called them for my refund of $20,500, they said that my son signed a contract stating that they hold my money for 365 days and I had to wait this waiting period, but he is welcome back anytime. How can they have an intoxicated addict sign a financial contract, he did not pay for the treatment. I scaped together all that money and now paying interest on it while they hold it and MAKE interest on it!! He refuses to go back because of his treatment there and I cannot afford to send him anywhere else. They are supposed to be helping these addicts, that is the opposite of what they are doing. one_star_reviews.text:
This is absolutely heartbreaking and, quite frankly, infuriating.
If you are going to operate a conservation foundation and make decisions involving wildlife, education about how these animals actually live, thrive, survive, and raise their young should be the bare minimum.
What I find incredibly disturbing is that the mother bear was killed, and now her yearlings are being moved to an unfamiliar environment without her. These aren't simply animals that can be treated like a problem and relocated without consequences. Bears have complex social behaviours, established ranges, survival skills, and strong family dynamics.
Before making decisions that permanently alter or end the lives of wildlife, I believe there should be serious consideration of every non-lethal alternative and the long-term consequences of those decisions.
I am absolutely disgusted by what appears to be a lack of understanding and compassion for these animals. Conservation should mean protecting wildlife not simply managing it when it becomes inconvenient for humans.
Educate yourselves. Do better. And most importantly, do better for the bears.

one_star_reviews.text:
I’ve been to this place four times, and after my last visit yesterday, I can officially say: apparently, customer service here comes with a dress code — white, skinny, and preferably someone the server already knows.

At first, I thought the server was simply having a bad day. I’m a server myself, so I understand that sometimes you’re tired, stressed, or just having one of those shifts. But four visits with exactly the same attitude? At some point, it stops being a bad day and starts looking like a personality trait.

I’m talking about the shorter, fair-skinned guy covered in tattoos. His customer service is practically nonexistent. Zero warmth, zero empathy, zero effort — but apparently an unlimited supply of friendliness when he’s serving people he actually likes.

Yesterday was the perfect example. I ordered a bottle of Prosecco. He brought me a rosé. And before I could even say, “Excuse me, I think this is the wrong bottle,” he simply dropped it on the table and walked away. No question, no apology, no acknowledgment. Just here’s your random wine, good luck.

Meanwhile, the girls at the table next to us — who appeared to be friends with him — were treated like VIPs at a five-star restaurant. Constant attention, smiles, checking on them, friendly conversation… basically a completely different server.

Meanwhile, we apparently had to submit a formal government application just to get him to look in our direction.

The difference in treatment was so obvious that it became uncomfortable to watch.

And yes, I’m going to say it: after experiencing this repeatedly, the way he treats people who don’t fit the “white and skinny” category feels deeply discriminatory and racist. Maybe that’s not the intention, but when the same behavior happens repeatedly and the contrast is this obvious, customers are going to notice.

What’s particularly disappointing is that I actually love this place. The reason I kept coming back was because I genuinely enjoyed it. Unfortunately, no food or atmosphere is good enough to make me want to repeatedly pay money to be treated like an inconvenience.

Management: maybe spend a little less time worrying about what’s happening on the menu and a little more time paying attention to what’s happening on the floor.

Because if this is the kind of service you’re comfortable providing, congratulations — you’ve managed to make a customer who actually liked your establishment seriously consider never coming back.

Four visits. Same attitude. Same treatment. Same server.

At this point, I don’t think he was having a bad day.

I think we were simply having the wrong skin tone.

I was jabed by a dirty needle while working. Work told me I needed to go and get preventative pills (pep) due to the high risk of the environment at the time. I went to a clinic that told me I had to go to emergency.
After the typical waiting period that comes with being in ER, I managed to see Dr. Auan. I told him what happened and talked about the emergency protocol of the preventative medication that was explained to me that was strongly recommended. Instead, he gave me more blood work and said we would see if I get a positive and review in a week. (You can't test positive with blood drawn the same day as exposure btw)
Essentially from my pov, Im told instead of going over options to protect me, let's see what happens and go from there.

I understand that you have to advocate for your own health sometimes, but when I did, the response was "that's just how we handle it". No explanation or assurance through communication about risk, or options.
I do trust that the doctors will do their best to act in a patients best interest, but I'll always argue that proper communication and developing a real mutual understanding goes a long way when it comes to actually addressing concerns of patients. Very disappointed..

Most nurses there are great people, they seem to understand our (the ppl's) frustrations. So everyone please understand that they genuinely work very hard and show a lot of compassion majority of the time which is very impressive and hard to always do with the workload they have.

Absolutely awful building management. This is not a review based on one isolated incident; unforunately, it reflects an ongoing pattern of issues that we have repeatedly brought to management’s attention without adequate resolution.

Our professional/medical building is currently on day THREE without toilet paper in the washrooms. Today we sent our secretary out to purchase toilet paper for our staff and clients. Imagine operating a professional business and having to hand a client a roll of toilet paper before they use the washroom. It is embarrassing and completely unacceptable.

Worse, this is not the first time this has happened. We have previously gone consecutive days without basic washroom supplies, despite notifying management. During the current incident, we have advised them daily and the problem still has not been remedied. I have the email correspondence documenting our complaints and the dates they were sent should anyone question the accuracy of this review.

Furthermore, the problems extend well beyond toilet paper. We have repeatedly raised concerns regarding building cleanliness, parking issues, washroom maintenance and other basic property-management matters, yet the same types of problems continue.

We understand that management may use third-party contractors for cleaning and other services; however, tenants should not have to chase contractors or repeatedly report the same deficiencies. The responsibility for ensuring those contractors are doing their jobs ultimately rests with the company being paid to manage the building.

When tenants repeatedly report problems and they continue unresolved, it is no longer an occasional oversight — it is a management problem.

For a professional/medical building, the overall standard of management, cleanliness and responsiveness has been extremely disappointing.

one_star_reviews.text:
I usually don’t write Google reviews, but I felt I had to this time because of the unprofessionalism and poor customer service I experienced at this branch.
Just this past week, I arrived at 3:50 p.m. and stood in line until I was finally helped at 4:25 p.m. There was a massive line with only two tellers serving customers. What made the experience even more frustrating was seeing employees walking around, yawning and discussing their next break in front of clients. I found this extremely disrespectful and unprofessional.
Interestingly, the branch has a sign displayed at the counters that says, “We bank on respect.” Respect goes both ways. If you expect respect from your clients, clients should be able to expect the same from your employees.
When I finally reached the teller and expressed my concerns, I was told that I could have simply used the ATM for my banking needs that day. Let’s make one thing clear: ATMs are not a solution for everyone. There are seniors who may not be comfortable using them, as well as customers who may have difficulty navigating technology or reading and understanding the prompts. Suggesting that everyone should simply use an ATM overlooks the fact that in-person banking is still an important and necessary service for many people.
What is even more disappointing is that I’ve seen negative reviews about this branch dating back several years, with similar generic responses from the bank such as, “We’re sorry for the frustration this may have caused.” Yet, if customers have been raising the same concerns for years, it’s fair to ask what meaningful action has actually been taken to address them.
Unfortunately, this experience has left me with a very negative impression of this branch and of TD’s customer service. I have personally had much better experiences at RBC branches, even when they are busy, where there seem to be enough employees available to manage large lines more efficiently.

I had the worst experience with Inga during my first pregnancy and postpartum period. My concerns were addressed with the staff at the time, but unfortunately, I never felt properly supported or listened to.

However, I had a very good experience with Nibal. She was very positive, answered all my questions and concerns, and took the time to listen to me, especially during the in-home visits. She was the only person on the team who I felt was doing her job properly. She was also very kind and caring, and I wish her all the best.

I ended up having a C-section, which my current midwives were surprised I had been allowed to have solely because of SPD. They questioned why it had been considered necessary in the first place. I felt that instead of taking the time to properly address my concerns, Inga simply referred me to an OB and essentially passed me along.

The postpartum care I received at Michael Garron Hospital was also extremely disappointing. They assumed I was allergic to Advil, so I was not given it as prescribed. Overall, I did not feel like I was receiving the level of care and attention I needed after giving birth.

No one properly helped me with breastfeeding. Everyone seemed to have a different method, which left me feeling confused, unsupported, and overwhelmed.

Even at my six-week postpartum appointment, I felt dismissed when I raised concerns about my baby crying constantly. I eventually asked to be discharged because of the way I felt I was being treated. I was told, “Newborns cry, you know that?” It turned out that my baby had a cow’s milk protein allergy. I wish my concerns had been taken more seriously instead of being brushed off.

Looking back, I really wish I had done more research before choosing where and with whom to receive my care.

I am now having my second baby at North York General Hospital with a team of midwives, and I can honestly say that my experience has been completely different. I feel supported, heard, and properly cared for. My current midwives told me they were surprised that I had been allowed to have a C-section just for SPD and questioned why it had been necessary.

The contrast between my first experience and my current care has been huge. I only wish I had received this kind of support the first time around.

Review posted on behalf of my Uncle Randy Humchitt - Bella Bella customer!
I was a loyal McKenzie Furniture customer for over 30 years. Although their prices were higher than some other places, I continued to shop with them because of the convenience of having my purchases delivered to Bella Bella. Over the years, I purchased furniture, appliances, and TVs from McKenzie.

Unfortunately, my experience with them recently has completely changed my view of the company.

I purchased a Maytag dryer from McKenzie, and when it broke down, I followed their recommendation and shipped it to a repair shop they suggested. Several weeks later, I was still waiting for the dryer to be repaired. When I contacted the repair shop, I was told they were still waiting for the parts needed to fix it.

I then contacted McKenzie Furniture. After looking around their warehouse for a couple of days, I was told that they had lost my dryer.

After being a customer for more than 30 years, I was extremely disappointed and upset. I expected better customer service, accountability, and communication from a business I had supported for decades.

The owner eventually offered to send me a new dryer, but only if I purchased another one from them at my own cost, with the shipping charges waived.

At that point, I decided I could no longer continue giving my business to McKenzie Furniture. After more than 30 years of loyalty, this experience was extremely disappointing.

I hope McKenzie takes this situation seriously and recognizes that customer service and accountability matter—especially when dealing with long-standing customers.

one_star_reviews.text: I've waited a full year to post my experience which was unfortunately not great during my actual labour and delivery with midwives. I loved my team and felt confident in their skills before going into labour. I was initially leaning towards a home birth and was told midwives were confident in this. I was low risk and a first time mom with a very "normal" pregnancy. Healthy, active etc. They asked all the right questions even my expectations during labour with a form which I wrote I have no idea what to expect as im a first time mom. Im choosing midwives to help guide me through that experience with their knowledge including positioning and breathing etc. I was told yes this is what we do. When it came to the actual labour I felt they were extremely uneducated . They did not encourage any positions or breathing or have any education when it came to babies engagement into the pelvis and or what I could be doing to help. I had pitocin contractions with no breaks to breathe and they had no problem encouraging the epidural and an in and out catheter. I didnt find them educated in physiological birth or even motivated to help me through it. I ended up with a c section which is fine if it had to be that way but I truly believe there was a disservice done and I want multiple children which now have other risks due to this. My daughter also ended up in the NICU, and I was discharged in 24 hours so I had no where to stay after major surgery to be near my daughter. When this was brought up it was brushed off as you weren't under our care anymore, call the hospital and make a formal complaint this happens and its frustrating. It just seemed like the things i chose them for to actually help me navigate was where they were lacking I've also learned since then they could've been proactive about my discharge date etc but it wasn't on their mind, so i shouldve advocated on my own, and knew better even as a first time mom. I'd say midwifery has a long way to go. If you go this route id recommend a doula  for your advocacy with birth and labour knowledge.

I had a disappointing experience with Niagara Midwives, which is unfortunate especially with a first pregnancy. I ended up switching over to an OBGYN and feel so much better with the care I am now receiving.

one_star_reviews.text:
You shouldn’t fear dying while in treatment like I did here. If you have serious medical issues, please think very carefully before choosing Trafalgar. I have epilepsy, and experienced repeated medication and safety failures during my stay. My family and I feel incredibly lucky that I came home alive.

Medication errors occurred 3+ times a week and resulted in two breakthrough seizures.

An NP changed my seizure-safety medication and told me I had agreed to a hospitalization protocol with the doctor and charge nurse—I had never met either of them. I was not given adequate time to contact my neurologist to correct the unauthorized changes, despite her knowing he is a co-founder of the Epilepsy Foundation. I was later told she was fired. I wish she had listened.

Clients’ medications were stored together in a plastic tote. After an RPN gave me incorrect medications three days in a row, her explanations included, “I can’t see” and “this is stressful.” When I expressed that a nurse should be able to safely dispense medication, she gave me the silent treatment for days until I apologized for being upset.

Despite asking daily, my seizure-safety plan wasn’t established until 10 days after I arrived. My roommates and I timed access to my rescue medication at approximately four minutes. This controlled medication was locked in the staff office and had to be retrieved and administered by support staff located nowhere near my room. My seizures often compromise my breathing. I was terrified I could have a nocturnal seizure and die waiting for help.

I lost count of how many times I went to management—pleading and crying—about my safety. The director promised my medications would be blister-packed because of the dispensing errors. That never happened. An hour before leaving Trafalgar, I was given another patient’s medication.

During my stay, an entire group of clients walked out of a session after a client was denied the opportunity to say goodbye to a dying immediate family member.

The food was wonderful, and the counsellors, therapists and RNs were phenomenal. One RN in particular may have saved my life by advocating for me when I felt I was no longer being heard. But that cannot outweigh what I experienced regarding medical safety.

People seeking treatment should not have to fear preventable medication errors or wonder whether lifesaving medication will reach them in time. I trusted Trafalgar with my health. I would not make that decision again.

I’ve been coming to this McDonald’s for a long time, and honestly, most of the staff—especially the night crew—are always friendly and treat me well. However, I’ve now had the same experience twice with the same employee.

My most recent experience happened on September 5 at around 1:04 AM. From my understanding, she is the only female employee working on the night shift, so I believe management should be able to identify who I’m referring to. She was speaking to me in a rude manner and seemed like she was always in a hurry, even though there wasn’t really a reason to rush the interaction.

I understand that restaurants can get busy, and I have no problem being patient, but basic respect and good customer service should still be there.

I was previously a manager at Wendy’s, so I understand what it’s like to work in a fast-food environment and how important it is to treat customers properly. This isn’t about expecting special treatment—it’s simply about being treated respectfully.

I don’t want to judge the entire location because the rest of the staff, especially the night crew, have always been nice to me. It’s just disappointing that I’ve now experienced the same behavior twice from the same person.

I hope management can look into this and address the situation because I genuinely like coming to this McDonald’s and would like to continue having good experiences here.

one_star_reviews.text:
Before Asr prayer today Aug 28, 2026 the Imam yelled at one of the young brothers over a minor issue — nothing that called for that kind of aggression from someone in his position. Allah reminds us that it was through gentleness, not harshness, that people remained close to the Prophet ﷺ:

“It is by the mercy of Allah that you were gentle to them. Had you been harsh and hard-hearted, they would have dispersed from around you. So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult with them in the matter. And when you have decided, then rely upon Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who rely upon Him.” (Surah Al Imran, 3:159) This matters even more with our youth, who already face so much misinformation online. They deserve correction delivered with a smile and respect, not yelling.

After the prayer, once most people had left, I approached him privately and told him what he had done wrong—that as an imam, he should have met the young brother with kindness and guided him gently instead of reacting aggressively. Instead of reflecting on this, he raised his voice at me too, insisting he had done nothing wrong, and asked me to leave the mosque. Allah describes the people He loves in this way:

"Those who spend in prosperity and adversity, and those who restrain anger and pardon people; and Allah loves the doers of good." — Surah Ali 'Imran, 3:134

I was honestly stunned that this was how an imam chose to respond. This didn't only affect me. Several of us were distracted during the prayer, still thinking about what had just happened, and I personally had to repeat my Asr prayer afterward. Having an Imam who does not understand what our youth are up against today, or how to take their hand and guide them toward the right path with patience, is a disgrace to this community. Allah instructs us:

"Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided." — Surah An-Nahl, 16:125

Whether the young brother was right or wrong in whatever he did barely matters now — the way he was spoken to was harsh enough to make him reluctant to ever set foot in the mosque again. Even Moses and Aaron, sent to confront Pharaoh, one of the most tyrannical men in history, were commanded:

"Speak to him gently, perhaps he will remember or fear [Allah]" — Surah Taha, 20:44
If Allah commanded gentleness even toward Pharaoh, a struggling young Muslim deserves nothing less.

I will not be returning to this mosque, nor will I continue to support it. I ask the community and board members to take this matter seriously. Allah says:

"Let there be among you a community inviting to good, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong. And it is they who are the successful." — Surah Ali 'Imran, 3:104

If this mosque's true purpose is to help and guide our youth—who are the future of this Ummah—then this cannot be overlooked.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very poor food quality, service, and staff response — management needs to address this
I’m leaving this review because this was far below what I would expect from McDonald’s, and unfortunately the issue was not just the food — it was the complete lack of acknowledgement or concern from the staff.
Date: August 29, around 8:00 PM.
I ordered McVeggie burgers and, when I opened them right in front of the staff, the burgers looked exactly like the photo attached. The patties were extremely dry, the burgers appeared poorly assembled, and there was very little dressing/sauce. They looked and tasted nothing like what you would reasonably expect from a freshly prepared McDonald’s burger.
I asked the staff member, “Can you put more dressing?” She responded as though she had no idea what I meant. I asked again — three times — and there was still no acknowledgement that anything was wrong with the burgers. I eventually had to clarify, “I mean sauce.” The response was essentially that they could give me sauce on the side.
That completely misses the point. If a customer opens a freshly served burger in front of you and says it is extremely dry and is asking for dressing, the appropriate response should be to look at the product, acknowledge the concern, and offer to correct the burger — not act as though there is nothing wrong and simply hand over sauce packets.
The service was equally disappointing:
We waited around 30 minutes or more for our order.
During that time, takeout orders appeared to be continuously coming out, including orders that seemed to have been placed before and after ours.
Customers who ordered through the kiosk after us were being served before us.
We had to ask about our order twice, with very little acknowledgement or urgency from the staff.
There was no clear communication about why our order was taking so long.
When we finally received the food, the quality was poor enough that we immediately raised the issue — and still felt completely ignored.
I understand that a restaurant can get busy. A long wait by itself would not be enough for me to leave a one-star review. What makes this experience unacceptable is the combination of the excessive wait, lack of communication, poor food preparation, and the staff's apparent unwillingness to acknowledge a very obvious customer complaint.
For the owner/management: please take this as constructive feedback and actually review what is happening during the evening shift. Staff need proper training on basic customer service, order prioritization, food assembly, and — most importantly — how to respond when a customer tells them there is a problem with their food. If additional training does not resolve the issue, management should seriously evaluate whether the current staffing and supervision are appropriate.
McDonald’s is a standardized fast-food operation. Customers should be able to reasonably expect consistent preparation, acceptable presentation, timely service, and basic acknowledgement when something goes wrong. None of those expectations were met during this visit.
The attached photo was taken when I opened the burgers in front of the staff and raised the issue, so this isn't a complaint based on how the food looked after being transported home. This is how the burgers were served to us, and staff were given an opportunity to see the problem and correct it.
One star. I hope management takes this seriously, because the biggest issue here wasn't simply a dry burger — it was the apparent lack of ownership when the problem was pointed out.

I’ve been coming to this Tim Hortons almost every day because I work in the mall, and unfortunately, the way I’ve been treated recently has made me completely uncomfortable coming back.

I usually order a very simple drink with a small modification. When I first started ordering it, I specifically asked if the modification wasn’t allowed and even said I was completely fine paying extra. I was told it was fine. A few weeks later, I was suddenly told by the manager that they were not allowed to make the modification because of “policy.” I completely understand if there is a policy against it, and I have no issue being told no.

What I do have an issue with is what happened afterward.

After that conversation, my drinks started being made incorrectly on multiple occasions. When I ordered no ice, my cup was repeatedly left significantly underfilled, even though the drink itself should have been filled to the appropriate level. This happened more than once, and given the timing and everything else I had been experiencing, it honestly felt intentional. I could have easily complained each time, but I chose not to because I didn’t want to argue with anyone over a coffee.

I also started noticing employees discussing my drinks whenever I came in and a clear change in their body language and attitude toward me.

The final straw was my most recent visit. I ordered something different from my usual drink, and while another employee was taking my order, the manager and employee laughed. They were standing right there in front of me, and I found it extremely disrespectful and embarrassing.

To be clear, I am NOT upset because they wouldn’t accommodate my modification. If there is a policy, I will respect it. What I am upset about is being treated differently afterward and receiving drinks that were repeatedly made improperly.

I used to come here almost every day because I work in the mall. I was a regular customer and had no problem spending my money here. Now I actively avoid this location because of how uncomfortable the staff have made me feel.

I really hope the person responsible for this location looks into what is happening. Customers should not be made to feel unwelcome or disrespected simply because they have a modification they regularly ask for.

I have lived in this apartment for almost 3 years. The apartment itself is not bad, but unfortunately, the management rules and services have been very disappointing.

1. Every summer, because of pest control, they come to inspect or treat the apartments. Each time, residents are asked to remove everything from the kitchen. This can be very difficult, especially for people who work long hours. After coming home tired from work, sometimes you just want to cook, eat, and sleep. It is frustrating that if you are not fully prepared when they come, you may be charged an additional fee.
2. The rent increases every year, but I have noticed that new tenants are sometimes offered apartments at cheaper prices than existing residents. I don’t understand why loyal tenants who have stayed for years end up paying more.
3. The parking lot does not feel safe. We pay for parking, but the security is very poor. I often leave early in the morning around 6 AM and regularly see cars with broken windows. This makes me feel that the parking area is not secure at all.

Overall, the apartment itself is okay, but the management policies, increasing rent, and lack of parking security have made my experience disappointing. I hope the management takes these concerns seriously and improves the service for residents.

I lived here for three years and just moved out. While the building itself is beautiful and a pretty great place to call home as far as the unit is concerned, with lots of amenities, beautiful views, and tons of stuff around, my review is for the building staff and management.

The staff at the concierge desk are truly terrible at their jobs and are very unfriendly/unhelpful. The only exception is the one guy that works at night, but the others pretty much just sit there and listen to music during their shifts or play on their phones, they are inconvenienced by anyone asking them anything, and they are entirely unreasonable and unhelpful in pretty much every situation. The management of the building is also very poor and disorganized; they double booked the elevator for my move out, and despite me and the other tenant who was also moving out figuring it out between us (they also informed me that the building messed up their schedule,) they provided no solution and got frustrated by the fact that I continued my move as scheduled. I had booked a truck already, hired movers, and had booked the elevator two weeks in advance—but they refused to acknowledge their mistake, claiming that the issue was on my end, despite the confirmation I had of the booking. The concierge staff member (Kevin) also screamed at me at the front desk and threatened to have my truck towed, despite the fact that my move didn’t disrupt anything (we never took over a full elevator at any point, and my truck was parked in the loading bay—as approved by the staff running the loading docks.) When I complained to office management, she changed the subject and instead tried to charge me $180 because apparently on August 20th my dog pooped in the dog run and they think I didn’t pick up after her—yet my dog and I weren’t even in the city at the time.

There are also regular fire alarms that go off in the building, lots of noise with outside bookings taking over the party rooms on the 7th floor, and frequent messes with people puking etc in the elevator.

Again, living here for 3 years was pretty decent for the most part, especially due to my landlord being awesome, but when it comes to anyone that works for Tridel—don’t expect them to do even the basics of their jobs and expect them to really put a damper on the living situation whenever they are involved in anything.

A message to the preacher of the second Friday sermon: Dear Sheikh, I hope you understand that some of the worshippers, myself included, have work, jobs, and meetings, and you live in a country where Friday is a workday.

Even if you say that worldly matters keep us busy, lengthening the sermon and shortening the prayer is contrary to the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). It is authentically reported from Ammar ibn Yasir (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “The length of a man’s prayer and the brevity of his sermon are signs of his understanding of the religion. So lengthen the prayer and shorten the sermons.” (Narrated by Muslim).

Lengthening the sermon and adding unnecessary details detracts from its essence, and people become bored. The proof is that people rush out after the prayer, indicating their boredom and that their hearts and minds are elsewhere. Indeed, Allah does not tire until you tire, as our noble Messenger said.

I urge you to consider people’s circumstances and make your sermons clear and concise, so that people do not become bored.

Very disappointed with my experience with Hoba. I visited last February. I have herniated a disk in the past and this has led to very tight hips. When Hoba did his visual inspection he blurted out "oh you have scoliosis". This came as quite a shock as I have never been told this, and have had imaging and x-rays on my back due to my herniation. To say something so flippantly as a health care professional is really worrying. This led to months of worrying and paying for further imaging to find out if I do in fact have scoliosis. I don't!! Do I have a small twist, yes. But absolutely not near the degree required for scoliosis. My posture is worse since herniating a disc because the muscles around my back have tightened to protect my back muscles.

You should know the weight of your words and use them carefully. Don't be so casual with your "diagnosis" next time.

one_star_reviews.text:
My vehicle was broken into at a different location, and several of my personal belongings were stolen, including my AirPods. I was subsequently able to track the AirPods using the tracking feature on my device, which indicated that they were located at or around this facility.

When I arrived at the facility, I spoke with the manager, who was helpful and made an effort to assist me in locating my AirPods. He explained that he was unable to search through everyone’s personal belongings, which I understood. I therefore attempted to locate the AirPods myself by using the detection feature and walking around the perimeter of the facility.

While I was doing this, a female employee approached me and asked what I was doing and whether I was looking for something. I explained the situation to her, including that my vehicle had been broken into at another location, that my belongings had been stolen, and that I was attempting to recover my AirPods because their tracking location indicated they were at or around the facility.

Unfortunately, unlike the manager who had attempted to assist me, she did not offer any meaningful assistance and instead told me that there was nothing I could do.

During our conversation, we discussed an analogy involving a bank. I asked her to consider the situation from this perspective: if someone committed a robbery and then brought or concealed stolen property inside a bank, would the fact that the bank was government-related or publicly funded mean that the stolen property would simply be ignored, or that the victim would be told to claim the loss through insurance?

She responded that, because the bank is part of the government, the bank would be able to offset the loss or deal with the situation itself. She then explained that, because this facility is also government funded, she did not believe the same analogy applied to my situation.

This is where I found her response particularly concerning. I understand that this facility operates as an injection site/harm-reduction facility and that its purpose is to provide services and support to the people who use the program. However, I do not understand how the nature of the facility or the fact that it is government funded would mean that stolen property being brought onto or located within the premises should not be taken seriously.

If someone were to commit a crime and subsequently bring stolen property into the facility, I do not understand why the nature of the facility would provide any exemption from addressing that situation. The fact that it is an injection site should not, in my view, mean that stolen property becomes the victim’s problem simply because it has been tracked to the premises.

I understand that the facility cannot search people’s belongings without appropriate authority, and I am not suggesting that staff should automatically accuse or search individuals. However, I was specifically telling a staff member that I had stolen property that I could actively track to the facility. I would have expected this to at least be taken seriously, with some form of reasonable assistance, investigation, documentation, or direction as to what could be done.

Instead, by the end of the conversation, I was essentially told that I would not be getting my AirPods back and that I should simply claim the loss through my insurance.

That response was extremely frustrating. What made the situation even more frustrating was that part of the explanation I was given relied on the claim that banks are government-owned. Canada’s major commercial banks, including RBC, TD, BMO, Scotiabank and CIBC, are publicly traded corporations owned by shareholders; they are not government-owned.

Ultimately, my concern is not simply about the value of a pair of AirPods. It is about the principle and the manner in which my concern was handled. I had stolen property that I could actively track to a facility, and rather than being provided with a meaningful course of action, I was essentially told that I should accept the loss and claim it through insurance.

At HSC, it feels like you have to constantly advocate, repeat yourself, and push to finally be heard. My best advice If you’re new to Winnipeg, an immigrant, have difficulty communicating in English, or simply don’t know how to advocate for yourself in a healthcare setting, please bring someone you trust with you or a translator. I am sharing this review so that future guests are aware of our experience and can make an informed decision before booking.

CMHA is not a hospital. Its employees are not automatically physicians or psychiatrists, and many cannot diagnose complex psychiatric illnesses or prescribe medication. Yet people experiencing suicidal thoughts, psychosis and other psychiatric emergencies are directed toward this charity system as though it were an acceptable replacement for medical care.
When staff lack the medical training and authority needed to treat the illness, the fallback too often becomes emergency services and police. For a terrified or suicidal person, sending police instead of providing immediate psychiatric treatment can escalate fear, trauma and danger.
This is what happens when a charity develops an institutional God complex: it places itself between seriously ill people and the qualified medical professionals they deserve.
Ontario’s official 2025 Sunshine List contains 276 CMHA employees earning at least $100,000. Their disclosed salaries total $36,566,663.99—and that does not include thousands of lower-paid employees or CMHA’s complete operating costs.
Multiplying Ontario’s disclosed amount by Canada’s ten provinces produces a rough national estimate of $365,666,639.90 per year. Because the provinces do not publish comparable CMHA records, this is an extrapolation rather than an audited total. The absence of a transparent national figure is part of the problem.
Imagine what hundreds of millions of dollars could accomplish if directed toward psychiatric hospitals, doctors, treatment beds, medication access and scientific research at institutions such as CAMH—a real teaching hospital employing physicians, psychiatrists, clinicians and researchers.
Instead, enormous amounts of money are absorbed by a fragmented charity network that cannot offer the medical authority or accountability of a hospital. Every dollar placed into this substitute system should be questioned when mentally ill people remain unable to see psychiatrists or obtain timely medical treatment.
If I have a heart attack, I deserve a doctor—not a charity worker.
If I am suicidal, psychotic or suffering from a serious psychiatric illness, I deserve exactly the same medical standard.
Mental illness is an illness. Stop replacing doctors with charities. Stop treating police intervention as psychiatric care. Fund hospitals, psychiatrists, medical treatment and real research.

In 2025 CMHA had 276 Ontario employees on the sunshine list taking an astronomical amount of $36.5 million with a average of $135,000 per employee. Imagine had that money gone to CAMH where it goes to doctors and actual research rather than the pockets of those scamming mentally ill and their supporters. Scam/fraud whatever you call it , they are sick people. Mentally ill people deserve the same level of care as physically ill and not second tier charity from those with God complexes at CMHA.

Misleading information, lack of clear communication, and complaining about taking calls on a designated emergency line is completely unacceptable. Management needs to address this lack of professionalism and fix their emergency response process immediately.

Based on my experience, I would **not recommend this property as a healthy or comfortable place to live**\. There have been serious concerns with **mold, mice, moisture, and insects**\. The property does not appear to have been properly renovated or maintained\.

I also have serious concerns about the **management and how maintenance issues are handled**\. My experience has left me feeling that management has not been transparent or responsive enough to residents’ concerns\.

Overall, I would strongly recommend that anyone considering this property **inspect the unit carefully for mold, moisture, pests, and the condition of the flooring and ceiling before signing a lease**\. I believe significant renovations and better property management are needed\.

Also, this doesn’t feel like an authentic Vietnamese restaurant. The fact that there wasn’t any cilantro at all was one of the first things I noticed. The noodles served with the bun cha and pho were exactly the same, and the noodles in the pho were even clumped together in the broth.

I ordered a combination of rare and well-done beef, but I honestly couldn’t tell the difference between the two. The vegetable toppings were also very sparse and chopped so finely that there was hardly anything there.

The water seemed to have been poured long before we arrived. The cups had apparently been sitting on the table with water in them for quite some time, which also made me question the restaurant’s overall hygiene.

The only positive things I can say are that the food came out very quickly after we ordered, and the first male cook/server who brought out our food was the only person who handled the dishes politely and actually wished us an enjoyable meal.

I recently visited this TD branch to have my debit card reissued. During the process, I was asked to provide my TD credit card and driver’s licence, which I did. I was also asked to verify a one-time passcode that was sent to my registered mobile number, and I received and confirmed it.

After completing all of these verification steps, I was told that I still had to wait for the manager to come and ask me additional security-related questions. I was honestly surprised and frustrated. I had already provided my TD card, government-issued driver’s licence, and successfully verified the one-time passcode sent to my registered phone number.

The manager eventually came and asked the security questions again, which I answered without any issue. However, the overall experience demonstrated a significant lack of efficiency, training, and common sense in handling a straightforward customer request.

I completely understand and support appropriate security procedures. However, customers should not be unnecessarily asked to repeat verification steps or wait for a manager when the required identification and authentication have already been completed.

This process unnecessarily wasted my time and made what should have been a simple debit-card replacement much more complicated than necessary. I strongly recommend that TD review its branch procedures and provide better training and clear guidelines to staff so that security requirements are handled consistently and efficiently while respecting customers’ time.

My response to SCHS's response. August 28, 2026

Initial Review 1 Star Aug 20, 2026
Having taken three years to get over my experience here I am now able to finally found the courage to review my stay here.

From being told that "I choose to believe" what I know happened to me and further more then told to NOT to the other people who were there,  this facility has no idea of how to handle complex trauma.

Complex trauma is NOT  what I choose to believe, it is remembering what actually happened to me as a child. If you look up complex trauma the best therapy is TALK therapy, NOT shut up and keep ot to yourself, because it is all in my head.

When I tell the other counselors what I was told they shake their head is disbelief.

This on top of conflicting diagnosis of CPTSD and ADHD, which any good therapist knows are very similar, and yes a person can have both, but one is the result of trauma and the other is not.

When I investigated going to SCHC, they told me they address my trauma. When I was there one of the program developers told me they are a first level, or introductory trauma centre. For the help I needed I had to go to a different centre. So I was misguided on my very first call.

Make sure you due your due diligence and find a centre, or even just a counselor if you are suffering from CPTSD.  Not one who tells you it is all in your mind, or to simply stop talking.

one_star_reviews.text:
If you are autistic and your needs don't exactly align with what a service provider expects, be cautious here.

I arrived at this service already knowing what I needed to function: a safe space and confirmation that things were safe before proceeding further. I hoped to receive new information and tools to better cope.

Instead, I was repeatedly pushed into psychoeducation aimed at developing skills I already possess. I was pressured to perform these skills even though they weren't meeting my actual support needs. Even though my clinical diagnosis is based on a 20-page report that clearly states I am often mute, they forced me to speak in stressful situations, which put me in a state where I could no longer access the skills I know I possess.

They broke protocol, even the law, by communicating with third parties on my behalf, against my explicit consent and instructions. When I asked for this to be rectified, I was instead told I needed more intervention to understand why it was the right thing to do.

When I tried to explain that this was rendering me unable to function and needed to be addressed first, the response wasn't to tackle the root cause. Instead, my experience was reframed as not being a real threat, or as being less serious than I described, and as requiring even more intervention in an already overloaded environment: the presence of a smoker, excessive perfume, noisy rooms, and a table arrangement that made me feel like I was in court before a judge, compounded by the fact that I was seated before several people at once, with multiple appointments being combined into one to save their own time.

They expected me to handle everything at once, which overwhelmed me, and when I asked for it to be spread out, they refused, stating that I was requesting too much time off or recovery. This is despite the fact that it's the number one need listed in my accommodation needs in my autism spectrum report.

This kind of reframing is offensive in itself, but it's also the opposite of helpful: it adds another layer of denial on top of a system that already fails to meet basic support needs.

I eventually became exhausted from having to defend myself to two people, and then went to CAAP Outaouais, who reviewed their emails and drafted a formal complaint on my behalf, documenting everything that was unethical and harmful in those emails alone.

I've never had a problem like this in my entire life, until I had to deal with the CISSSO in Buckingham. You'd think a division specializing in ASD would be more competent, but no. Perhaps they rely too heavily on their training in Intellectual Disability: ID-ASD (Intellectual Disability-Autism Spectrum Disorder).

The mere fact that the organization associates autism with intellectual disability is an affront to all autistic people.

one_star_reviews.text: Our elevator renovation was started in February. It was promised to be finished at the beginning of May. We were fine with the two-month renovation as it was normal. In the midst of May, we received an email stating that it would be delayed. We were fine still but slightly frustrated. Unfortunately, we were not prepared for the future. It kept getting delayed through June and July, and they were barely working on it at times. We received no service and help, sometimes taking stuff downstairs, and my father, with back problems who got better, started having pain again. We tried to file a complaint, but it went nowhere. It continued to get delayed with excuses until August, where enough people complained that they temporarily opened it. However, to our surprise, it shut down for maintenance after a week. Again, it continued to stay on for a week max and be closed again. My father had to take two months off work due to his back pain being unbearable, and he was not able to leave the house at times. I am currently writing this in September, and our elevator shut down again. This is my second review, and I will continue as this management is absolutely horrible. Our experience from living in this building has been phenomenally bad. And the management has done absolutely nothing.
